record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of infinite dimensional algebras
record.context_brief: SL(3,Z) group algebra and property tau
record.original_question: Let K be a field of characteristic zero. Does the group algebra K[SL(3, Z)] satisfy algebraic property tau in the sense that some finite-dimensional generating subspace S expands every finite-dimensional subspace W of every infinite-dimensional residually finite K[SL(3,Z)]-module with no nonzero finite-dimensional submodules by a uniform factor greater than 1?

evidence.quote: We even don't know an answer to the following question. Problem 11. Let K be a field of zero characteristic. Does the group algebra K[SL(3, Z)] satisfy tau?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero and let $\Gamma = SL(3,\mathbb{Z})$. The group algebra $K[\Gamma]$ is said to satisfy the algebraic property $\tau$ if there exists a finite-dimensional $K$-subspace $S \subseteq K[\Gamma]$ that generates $K[\Gamma]$ as an algebra, together with a constant $\varepsilon > 0$, such that for every $K[\Gamma]$-module $M$ that is

(i) infinite-dimensional over $K$,
(ii) residually finite-dimensional (i.e., the intersection of all finite-codimension submodules is zero), and
(iii) has no nonzero finite-dimensional submodule,

and for every finite-dimensional $K$-subspace $W \subseteq M$, one has
$$\dim_K(S \cdot W) \;\geq\; (1+\varepsilon)\,\dim_K W.$$

Question: Does $K[SL(3,\mathbb{Z})]$ satisfy the algebraic property $\tau$?
